history.summary: THIN DOCUMENTATION — the Chaturbhuj Temple inside Maihar Fort is attested only in tourism write-ups, which describe it as an ancient temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu within the fort complex. No reliable source found for its builder, dynasty, or date, and no temple-specific hours, festivals, or web footprint exist. Do NOT confuse it with the Chaturbhuj temples of Orchha (16th c.), Khajuraho (c.1100 CE), or Gwalior Fort (c.875 CE, famous for the early zero inscription). Coordinates are town-level only (geocoder matched the Maihar district locality, not the fort temple itself) — treat as APPROXIMATE.

name: Chaturbhuj Temple, Maihar Fort
town_description: Maihar is a town in Madhya Pradesh dominated by the Maa Sharda Devi temple atop Trikuta Hill (1,064 steps and a ropeway since 2009), a major Shaktism pilgrimage site. It was the former capital of the princely state of Maihar (founded 1778) and the birthplace of the Maihar gharana of classical music founded by Ustad Allauddin Khan. The hilltop Maihar Fort complex, about 1.5 km from Maihar railway station, houses several old shrines including this Chaturbhuj temple.

travel.road: Well connected by road; ~35 km from Satna, ~45 km from Khajuraho (verify)
